why: The loop uses i <= n instead of i < n, so it runs one extra time: it reads 4 bytes past the checked header and writes ids[n], one past the end of ids when n == ids_size (off-by-one overflow).

why: count is checked against SIZE_MAX / sizeof(*dst) before the multiply, so count * sizeof(*dst) cannot overflow, and malloc failure is handled, so memcpy always fits in dst.
